Data Storytelling

Data Story Tracking System

This module tells the story of your data’s journey by: 1. Recording each chapter of your data’s life 2. Capturing the essence of your data at each moment 3. Maintaining a chronicle of changes 4. Sharing the story with your team

The goal is to make data changes as readable as a story, helping everyone understand how data evolves over time.

data_storyteller.begin_new_story()[source]

Start a new data story by creating the initial settings.

Like any good story, we need to decide if it’s a solo adventure or a collaborative tale.

data_storyteller.capture_data_essence(df)[source]

Distill the essence of our data into a memorable summary.

Like a book summary, we capture: - How many characters (rows) are in our story - The key themes (numeric patterns) that emerge

data_storyteller.create_memory_imprint(essence)[source]

Create an unforgettable impression of this moment in data’s story.

Like a book’s ISBN, this unique identifier helps us: - Remember exactly how the data looked - Spot when the story changes - Keep track of different editions

data_storyteller.read_previous_chapters()[source]

Recall what happened in previous chapters of our data story. Returns an empty book if this is where the story begins.

data_storyteller.share_story(filepath, memory, settings)[source]

Share our data’s story with other readers.

In collaborative mode: The story goes to a shared library In solo mode: We keep the story in our personal collection

data_storyteller.tell_story_of_changes(filepath, previous_edition, new_essence)[source]

Narrate how our data’s story has evolved.

Tells the tale of: - Which part of our data changed - How the numbers shifted - When this new chapter began

data_storyteller.write_new_chapter(chronicle)[source]

Add a new chapter to our data’s story.

The data_storyteller module provides functionality for creating comprehensive narratives about data changes:

  • Change storytelling

  • Trend analysis

  • Impact assessment

Example Usage

from data_storyteller import DataStoryteller

# Create a storyteller instance
storyteller = DataStoryteller()

# Generate a story about data changes
story = storyteller.tell_story('data.csv')

# Print the story
print(story)
